clue.text: How building is laid out as intended

definitions.meaning: a building goes up following the architect's drawings, the way it was designed on paper
happening just as was meant or arranged

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both following the architect's drawings and, figuratively, going exactly as arranged beforehand.

clue.text: Without a squeak?

parts.note: making no squeak at all, like the small rodent that squeaks being totally silent

explanation.surface: A question about something that makes no noise, perhaps a well-oiled door.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile describes someone utterly silent, likened to a timid rodent creeping about noiselessly.

clue.text: Non-paying offence, so it is said

definitions.text: Non-paying offence, so it is said

parts.words: Non-paying offence, so it is said
parts.note: an offence that, by the old proverb, never pays its perpetrator

explanation.surface: Someone describes a minor offence such as fare-dodging.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'it doesn't pay' gives 'Non-paying ... so it is said'; 'offence' is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal act is an offence against the law, and the saying insists such wrongdoing never pays.

clue.text: Political favour

parts.note: a favour here is a ribbon badge, the kind worn by party candidates and supporters

explanation.surface: Looks like a politician doing someone a good turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'favour' means a token, a knot of ribbon worn as a badge, not a kindness; candidates at British elections wear one in party colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon badge in party colours is the favour worn by election candidates.

clue.text: Not accurate in former part of play

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
an act is a division of a play

explanation.surface: Someone complains that an early scene of a drama gets its facts wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imprecise is not accurate.

clue.text: Minimum cover on which an air might be played

definitions.meaning: the skimpiest of undergarments, covering very little

definitions.text: on which an air might be played
definitions.meaning: the lowest violin string, from Bach's famous Air arranged by Wilhelmj

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a skimpy piece of underwear and the violin string of the well-known 'Air on the G String'.

clue.text: Smother relievo pattern

indicators.note: a pattern is an arrangement, so the letters of relievo are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: An artist covers up a raised relief design.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie on top of something, such as an infant, can smother it.

clue.text: German count to alight unsmiling

parts.note: to alight is to come down and land
grave means serious, unsmiling

explanation.surface: A stern German nobleman stepping down from a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Landgrave was a count with territorial jurisdiction in the Holy Roman Empire.

clue.text: This combination might well have you in stitches

definitions.text: This combination might well have you in stitches

parts.words: This combination might well have you in stitches
parts.note: in stitches suggests helpless laughter, but here a sewing pair literally puts stitches in

explanation.surface: A comic double act guaranteed to make you laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp sewing tool threaded with thread is the pairing used to make stitches.

clue.text: Still leave out riotous scene

indicators.note: leave out read as the word for leave placed outside the rest

parts.note: to quit is to leave

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters of scene are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone stays motionless, refusing to leave a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' puts QUIT round ESCEN, the anagram of SCENE signalled by 'riotous'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiescent means inactive or at rest, like something still.

clue.text: Bondsman?

parts.note: the 'man' who picks the bonds: the machine choosing winning Premium Bond numbers

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about a person standing surety, or a serf.
explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are a British savings scheme with prize draws; the winning numbers are generated by a machine known by a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment selects the winners of Britain's Premium Bonds prizes.

clue.text: Still one article on sluggishness

parts.note: inert means motionless, still
I is the Roman numeral for one
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A remark on someone's remaining piece of writing about laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to stay at rest, i.e. sluggishness.

clue.text: Gail and Ella endlessly drunk contrary to law

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and reeling, so the letters are jumbled
endlessly means the last letter of Ella is cut off

explanation.surface: Two women are tipsy, perhaps while under age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims ELLA to ELL; 'drunk' then shuffles GAIL with ELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illegal is against the law.

clue.text: About to put on a trick

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is just about to play a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A con is a swindle, a trick.

clue.text: Violent storm experienced by noted member in the river

indicators.note: in places the member inside the river

parts.note: the Test is a famous trout river in Hampshire
an MP is a Member of Parliament
E is a musical note, so noted adds a note

explanation.surface: A celebrated politician caught in a squall while on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a Hampshire trout river, a crossword favourite; 'noted member' is MP with a note, E, after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent windy storm.

clue.text: Preserve the colour of some cats

definitions.meaning: a preserve is jam or a similar conserve, here the orange kind
ginger tabby cats are so called for their orange fur

explanation.definitionFit: It names both the citrus conserve and the orange-ginger shade of tabby cats.

clue.text: He sounds a bright lad

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word is identical in speech to another

parts.note: the sun is a bright one in the sky

explanation.surface: A boy who comes across as clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bright' tempts as clever, but it is the shining star in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child, a lad.

clue.text: Potential danger near a Caribbean island

indicators.note: potential suggests the letters of danger could become something else

explanation.surface: A warning that a holiday island holds hidden risks.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is an island nation in the West Indies.

clue.text: Artie trapped you, say, in a fur row

indicators.note: trapped means the letter for you is held between the others

parts.note: the name Artie is pronounced like the letters R and T
the letter U is pronounced like you

explanation.surface: A man called Artie catches you at a row over a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fur row' is to be read as furrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A rut is a groove or furrow, as made by wheels.

clue.text: One helping to restore taverns

indicators.note: to restore is to rebuild, so the letters of taverns are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker who helps refurbish pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant is someone employed to help in a household.

clue.text: See an incision made first sharply

indicators.note: made first says the incision piece comes before the other

parts.note: a cut is an incision
Ely is a cathedral city, and a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A surgeon tells someone to watch an incision being made.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, is the crossword's favourite bishop's see.
explanation.definitionFit: Acutely means keenly or sharply.

clue.text: Venetian artist to draw the game

parts.note: a tie is a drawn match
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A painter from Venice is asked to sketch a sporting match.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an eighteenth-century painter from Venice.

clue.text: A living wage

parts.note: a living is a church benefice, so this is the pay that comes with a parish post

explanation.surface: Seems to be the slogan for pay enough to live on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'living' is a clergyman's benefice, not subsistence.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is the fixed salary of a clergyman, the income of his living.

clue.text: Scream on seeing a mass of debris on the church

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: scree is loose stony debris on a mountainside
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone screams at seeing a pile of rubble on the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a harsh, shrill scream.

clue.text: One possessing a particular ad vantage getting in the drink, we hear

definitions.text: One possessing a particular ad vantage

parts.note: taken as being in, inside

indicators.note: we hear signals a word as spoken, not as written

parts.note: cider is an apple drink

explanation.surface: A drinker with an edge, perhaps from getting into the cider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ad vantage' is the printed split of advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider has privileged knowledge from within a group, a special advantage.

clue.text: Shortly incorporating the American company

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short to its standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A firm is being taken over soon by a US company.
explanation.walkthrough: Inc, for incorporated, follows the name of a US company as Ltd does a British one.
explanation.definitionFit: Inc is the suffix marking an American incorporated company.

clue.text: Foot step

definitions.meaning: a foot is a metrical unit in verse and a unit of length
a step taken to achieve something, as in drastic action

explanation.definitionFit: Both a unit, such as a foot of verse or length, and a course of action taken.

clue.text: Gentleman back to return to the dish

indicators.note: back means the title is read from the end

parts.note: sir is the title for a gentleman

indicators.note: to return means the word to is turned round

explanation.surface: A gentleman goes back to send back a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A risotto is an Italian rice dish.

clue.text: A rest was disturbed by the crying

indicators.note: disturbed means upset or rearranged, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone's nap was interrupted by a wailing baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Tears are what crying produces.

clue.text: Edict on United Kingdom sea disaster

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so the letters of sea are broken up

explanation.surface: A decree issued about a British shipwreck.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was a decree of the Russian tsar, so any arbitrary edict.

clue.text: Current of air on medico behind

parts.note: on and over both mean above or upon
DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medico
aft means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A draught blows over a doctor's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current of air' reads as a draught, but only 'Current' defines: the bank account that can go into the red.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft is a debit on a current account at the bank.

clue.text: These morons very confused with all of us

indicators.note: confused means muddled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Insulting some idiots, the speaker admits we are all just as muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means each and every person, without exception.
